%1$d below your last take. Each repeat still counts.
The "th" in "think": put the tip of your tongue between your teeth and blow softly.
The voiced "th" in "this": tongue between the teeth, with your voice buzzing.
The "s" in "sun": tongue just behind your teeth, a steady hiss.
The "z" in "zoo": like "s" but with your voice buzzing.
The "sh" in "she": tongue a little back, lips slightly rounded, a soft hiss.
The "ch" in "cheap": a quick "t" followed by "sh".
The "j" in "jeep": a quick "d" followed by the voiced "sh".
The "r" in "right": curl or bunch your tongue back without touching the roof.
The "l" in "light": touch the roof behind your teeth with the tongue tip.
The "w" in "west": round your lips, like a quick "u".
The "v" in "vest": lower lip against the upper teeth, with voice.
The "b" in "best": press both lips together, then release with voice.
The "ng" in "sing": the back of your tongue rises to the soft palate, air through the nose.
The "n" in "sin": tongue tip behind the teeth, air through the nose.
The short "i" in "ship": relaxed and quick.
The long "ee" in "sheep": stretch it and smile.
The "a" in "bad": jaw open wide, lips relaxed.
The "e" in "bed": jaw a little open, lips relaxed.
The "u" in "cup": short, central, relaxed.
The "o" in "cop": mouth open wide, sound at the back.
The short "oo" in "pull": short and relaxed, lips slightly rounded.
The long "oo" in "pool": round your lips firmly and stretch it.
The "aw" in "bought": open and rounded, from the back of the mouth.
The "o" in "boat": glide from "o" to "oo".
The "a" in "late": glide from "e" to "ee".
The "h" in "house": breathe out before the vowel.
The nasal "an" in "dans": open, unrounded, air through the nose.
The nasal "on" in "bon": lips rounded, air through the nose.
The nasal "in" in "vin": tongue forward, unrounded, air through the nose.
The nasal "un" in "brun": lips rounded, tongue forward, air through the nose.
The French "u" in "tu": say "ee" and round your lips.
The closed "eu" in "peu": round your lips while saying "e".
The open "eu" in "peur": lips rounded, jaw dropped a little.
The French "r" in "rue": a soft rub at the back of the throat, not rolled.
The "j" in "je": like "sh" but with voice.
The "gn" in "agneau": the middle of your tongue against the palate.
The "ui" in "nuit": a quick glide from rounded to front.
The light "e" in "petit": a soft "uh", passed over quickly.
